newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says 200 tonnes of aid received after quake.
newsitem.headline: Iran says 200 tonnes of aid received after quake.

text.p: International aid sent to Iran for survivors of last weekend's deadly earthquake which left 50,000 homeless has reached the 200 tonne mark, Tehran radio said on Thursday.
It said emergency food and other aid delivered by 16 countries after Saturday's quake reached 200 tonnes on Wednesday, up on 130 tonnes the previous day.
The radio did not name the donor countries.
The United Nations had donated $810,000 for medicines, it said.
Some 750 truckloads of aid collected in Iran had been sent to the remote villages devastated by the quake which measured 7.1 on the Richter scale, the radio said.

A U.N. report released in Tehran on Wednesday listed the latest donations as an air consignment from the relief charity Oxfam that included 750 emergency shelters, a plane load of aid from Spain, a $128,000 pledge from Sweden and relief items worth $150,000 from Greece.

Rasul Zargar, Iran's top official in charge of natural disasters relief, said latest casualty figures showed 1,568 people had been killed, 2,300 injured and 15 were missing, the Iranian news agency IRNA said on Thursday.
Iran said on Tuesday the quake killed 1,560 people and injured 2,810.
Zargar said the quake had levelled or heavily damaged 168 villages.
Relief workers had set up 12,000 tents in these areas for the survivors, he added.

An aftershock measuring 5.6 on the Richter scale, the strongest of 250 recorded since Saturday's quake, jolted the quake-stricken area on Tuesday, killing one person and destroying 10 houses, IRNA said.
An earthquake measuring 4.2 on the Richter scale hit the northwestern province of East Azerbaijan on Wednesday, but there was no immediate word on casualties, it said.
Earthquakes of force four or more are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in a populated area.

Algeria's Red Crescent said on Wednesday it would contribute $100,000 to help the quake victims. Algeria broke diplomatic ties with Iran in 1993, accusing Tehran of supporting Moslem rebels fighting the Algerian government.

The Geneva-based International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies has said it has raised seven million Swiss francs ($4.6 million) towards its 12 million Swiss franc appeal to help the quake victims.
The money was raised from four governments -- Britain, Denmark, the Netherlands and Norway -- and from 13 national Red Cross or Red Crescent societies.
Several other countries have made pledges or said they have sent aid, including Iran's arch-foe the United States and European Union states involved in a diplomatic row with Tehran.
